root_idea.summary: The root centers on expelling air and the resulting inflation or swelling, with extensions to elevation, vigor, and figurative pride.
root_idea.development: The evidence connects blowing with physical inflation and swelling, then extends the imagery to elevated daylight, fertile spring growth, fatness, arrogance, and related bodily or environmental states.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested Form I verb has distinct lexical uses for blowing air and breathing spirit into creation.
The Quran-attested feminine noun is a distinct lexical item meaning a blast, specifically the eschatological trumpet blast.

senses.definition: To blow air or wind into or onto something; in trumpet contexts, to produce the blast by blowing into the instrument.
senses.usage_conditions: Used for active blowing and passive being blown. Quranic constructions include blowing into a trumpet and blowing upon an object such as the heated iron in 18:96.

senses.definition: To breathe spirit into a created being.
senses.usage_conditions: A specialized construction with the spirit as what is breathed into the created being; the Quran applies it to the first creation and to the creation of Jesus.

senses.definition: A blast, specifically the blast of the resurrection trumpet.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic occurrence, the noun denotes the eschatological trumpet blast rather than bodily inflation or an ordinary breath.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To incite someone to aspire to what is not his due.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic, figurative expression describing the devil's blowing into a person's nose.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To puff out the sides of the mouth in pride; to act arrogantly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use of bodily inflation for affected pride.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause someone or something to become inflated or filled by food.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive use describing the effect of food on the body.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have wind-swollen testicles, or to have pasterns swollen with wind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a man or horse for swollen testicles and to a beast of carriage for wind-swollen pasterns.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To emit intestinal gas or flatulence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A bodily use describing the emission of abdominal wind.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For the wind to arrive suddenly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive use applied to the sudden onset of wind.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a road to cast or bring travelers suddenly to a place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension from the wind's sudden movement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For the morning or day to advance, with the sun becoming high.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression refers to the later morning, approximately an hour before noon.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become inflated, puffy, or swollen; to become filled by food.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The intransitive Form VIII counterpart of bodily or object inflation, including swelling from food.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The swelling or growing large of the new moons.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional expression used in an account of last-day signs.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become puffed up against someone; to grow angry or behave angrily toward him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative Form VIII construction with عَلَى or لِ describing anger.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Flatulence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verbal noun used as a bodily noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Boastfulness, arrogance, or pride.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension expressed also in the phrase ذُو نَفْخٍ, a person inflated with pride.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A youthful, full-bodied young person; specifically a young man, and without the feminine suffix, a damsel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An archaic descriptive noun emphasizing youthful fullness or vigor.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An inflation of the belly or body, including a flatulent humor.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A bodily swelling or distension caused by food or another humor.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A slight odor.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Distinguished from نَفْحَةٌ, which denotes a more plentiful odor.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The prime or productive surge of youth or spring.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In the youth expression it is the chief part of youth; in the spring expression it is the phase when vegetation is produced or has reached its seasonal fullness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A disease causing a horse's testicles to swell.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A veterinary use distinct from ordinary bodily inflation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Elevated, soft, fertile, or tumid ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to land with elevation and productive soil, including earth that breaks into pieces when trodden upon.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The upper part of the shank or tibia.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One employed to blow a fire.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An agent noun for a person tending a fire by blowing it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A disease-caused inflation or humor arising in any part of the body.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A pathological bodily swelling or the humor producing it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bubble upon water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A small inflated body formed on the surface of water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The air bladder of a fish.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The inflated internal structure said to help the fish rise and move in the water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bladder or inflated cell of a plant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a plant bladder and, in anatomical terminology, to a cell.

other_classical_meanings.definition: No one is in the house.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiom literally referring to there being no blower of a fire in the dwelling.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man puffed up and ready to cause mischief or harm.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic description of someone inflating his sides in readiness for hostile action.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having wind-swollen testicles, or having pasterns swollen with wind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a man or horse for swollen testicles and to a beast of carriage for affected pasterns.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man full of flaccid fat or corpulent flesh.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A descriptive noun or adjective for fatness characterized as inflation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An instrument for blowing a fire or other object, especially a blacksmith's bellows.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The instrument into which one blows or with which a fire is blown.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A shepherd's reed pipe used to call camels together.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized blowing instrument, distinct from a blacksmith's bellows.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The suggestions or promptings of the devil.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative plural expression based on the devil's blowing or inflation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Big-bellied or fat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An epithet for a body inflated or swollen with fat.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A coward.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use explained through the image of one swelling out his lungs.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Puffed up or inflated with pride or anger.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative Form VIII participle describing an emotionally inflated person.

cautions: The Form I verb has two Quran-attested branches that should not be collapsed: blowing air into or onto an object, and breathing spirit into a created being.
Lane's historical Quran citation notation in the physical-blowing entry has not been converted into a modern verse location; modern examples use only independently supplied QAC locations.
